As shown in Fig. 4, when the laser power is 0 W, the surface quality is the worst.
The main surface defects are pits, scratches, and SiC particle breakage.
With the in-situ laser assistance, the defect size is significantly smaller, and the ductile removal area is larger.
When the laser power increases to 4 W and 6 W, there are no large-sized pits and scratches caused by particles pulled-out.

When the interaction force between the diamond tool and the SiC particles is greater than the bonding force at the interface, the particles would be pulled out, forming pits.
This is the main form of material removal in conventional diamond cutting.

In addition, when the pulled-out or broken SiC particles are attached to the tool flank face, they move relative to the workpiece under the diamond tool extrusion, forming scratches on the machined surface.
In the in-situ laser assisted diamond cutting, the laser beam is directly irradiated on the cutting area, heating and softening the material to be removed.
